findings.reason: §3 is the plan's most expensive section (1.25h across five write sites) and its case rests on a population roughly 40x larger than the spellings it proposes to add, so a correct figure changes both the motivation and the section's priority.
findings.text: the "more than 400 across 19 plans, 59 in shared-coil-supply-model alone" figure is presented as the prevalence of deferred-work prose, but it is a count over power-convertor-df's census pattern (power_convertor/docs/briefs/prose-follow-on-audit.md:24), which is dominated by `follow-on` — the one spelling reckon already refuses; measured in that checkout, `follow-ons?` occurs 501 times across docs/plans/ in 19 plans and 76 times in shared-coil-supply-model, against 2 occurrences of `carry to §N`, 6 of `go(es) to §N` and 1 of `go(es) to a follow-up node`

findings.reason: a builder implementing the regex as written delivers a rule that still misses roughly 40 occurrences in the corpus the section cites, so the section's own claim of completeness is unmet by its mechanism and the regex must carry the past-tense form at least.
findings.text: §3 is titled "the deferred-work rule reads every spelling" and proposes covering `carry|carries to §N`, `go|goes to §N` and `go|goes to a follow-up (node|section|plan)`, but the census this section is drawn from patterns `carr(y|ies|ied) (forward|to)` as well as `left for|later node|next node|separate node|deferred to|for a later|followon|follow on`, and those spellings are present today in power_convertor's docs/plans/ — `carried to §N` 4 times, `next node` 9, `followon` 5, `later node` 2, `separate node` 2, `left for` 2, `follow on` 2, `deferred to` 1 — all of which the declared mechanism leaves unreported and unrefused

findings.reason: no done-when case turns on `top`, and the refusal behaves correctly for that anchor whether or not it is reserved, so the sentence overstates a property rather than directing a wrong implementation.
findings.text: §4 asserts "Both sets carry `top`", but defines the rendered set as the plan's comment keys plus the current ledger runs' section keys; a plan with no plan-level comment has no `top` key, so the rendered set would not carry it and the reserved set (rendered plus plan sections plus `outcome`) would not either unless `top` is added explicitly

findings.reason: the quotes are illustrative and every other part of §1's root cause reproduces, so the correction is to the citation, not to the work.
findings.text: §1 says "Followup bodies and close comments in power_convertor carry phrases such as ... `the remaining non-blocking items go to a follow-up node`", but that phrase occurs zero times in any plan, comment or followup in that checkout and only in power_convertor/docs/briefs/prose-follow-on-audit.md:11, where it is given under "Examples include:" rather than as a located hit

findings.reason: each symbol is named exactly and resolves by grep, so the hints cost a builder one search and point at no renamed or deleted target.
